Before the Gates of Paradise

Story

The last choice, made at the threshold.

Climbing the wide white stairs, I see a great golden gate. Having passed the judgment, I have been let through. Now all that is left is to walk through the gate, but I stop. Beyond it I see eternal peace and union with everything, but the habit of the mortal world holds me.

I agreed to constant struggle in life. My contest seemed so long that I had said goodbye to peace. Once I enter Paradise, there will be nothing more: no falls and rises, no misfortune and happiness, no pain and relief. Nothing like that will ever be in my head again.

Life brings misfortune, but because of it I can tell happiness apart, and so I will be at peace. I am used to the earthly swings of fate and would not like to leave them. After entering, I will not exist for myself, but I will still exist. I think it is worth connecting with everything through earthly feelings.

I pass through the gate and enter Paradise.
